bug_semantics: An unauthenticated federated ActivityPub server can send a Create/Note whose sanitized content contains an emoji shortcode and whose attacker-controlled Emoji tag supplies icon.url and name. NodeBB replaces the shortcode after the content sanitization pass with an HTML img string containing those values in quoted attributes, then stores that generated HTML. The remote-post display path can return the stored HTML without a subsequent markdown/sanitize-html pass, so an attribute-breaking value becomes persistent same-origin XSS for viewers. The first exploitable sink interpolated icon.url; commit 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 subsequently added the unescaped title from tag.name.
flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6: it first added the incoming ActivityPub emoji rewrite to src/posts/create.js and directly interpolated tag.icon.url into an img src immediately before post storage. Its parent has no emoji rewrite or tag.icon.url use in that file. Commit 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 is only a later refactor that moved the already-vulnerable construction into Helpers.renderEmoji, so it is not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6` shows author and committer Julian Lam <julian@nodebb.org>, one parent, and only the message `feat: #12683, parse incoming emoji tags and replace in content prior to storage in database`; it has no Co-authored-by/Generated-with trailer and no bot identity.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/NodeBB/NodeBB/issues/14601 documents the remote inbox -> notes.assert -> Mocks.post flow, pre-render sanitization, post-render storage, remote display bypass, PoC result, and the unescaped src/title sink; GHSA-fh4m-97qj-ff6c references direct patch c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e and v4.15.0. In the clone, `git show 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 -- src/posts/create.js` shows the new replacement `` immediately before the existing create hook and db.setObject. `git show 4ba41a68011c7151925bfcbf3ab6168e97c9d893:src/posts/create.js` shows the parent proceeds from the optional ActivityPub URL assignment directly to the create hook/storage, and `git grep -n 'tag\.icon\.url' 4ba41a68011c7151925bfcbf3ab6168e97c9d893 -- src/posts/create.js` has no match (exit 1), directly verifying parent absence. `git log --reverse -S'tag.icon.url' -- src/posts/create.js` returns 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 as the first addition and 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3 as its later removal during refactoring; `git log -L 50,66:src/posts/create.js bb5e711802746ae130281d02a838f2a9102ea27e` independently traces the sink to 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6. `git show 3968c822a2291d32d79a86ba625858a90e8496f9 -- src/posts/create.js` shows title="${tag.name}" was added the following day. `git show 9608cce693d43579b54ef2500133f0630f7a96c3` shows the helper extraction retained the same raw src/title construction, confirming it was a move rather than an introduction. `git show c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e` shows the direct advisory patch adds `if (!Helpers.isUri(tag.icon.url)) return;` before rendering; Helpers.isUri uses validator.isURL with a required protocol/host and accepted ActivityPub protocols. Release ancestry is reproducible with `git tag --contains 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6` (first containing release v4.0.0-rc.1), `git merge-base --is-ancestor 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6 v3.12.9` (exit 1), `git merge-base --is-ancestor c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e v4.14.10` (exit 1), and the same command against v4.15.0 (exit 0). Thus the vulnerable implementation first shipped in v4.0.0-rc.1, remained through v4.14.10, and the advisory-designated patch first shipped in v4.15.0. The direct patch validates icon.url but does not escape title's tag.name; no validator.escape addition appears in the patch, so the name-attribute portion described by the issue is not independently closed by this commit even though it is the advisory's declared fix boundary.
reasoning: The causal first writer is the ordinary single-parent feature commit 09b1e11940bebab92bbb48c8a1e1714fc9e95ea6, not the 2026 helper refactor: the former created the unsafe post-storage HTML sink and its immediate parent directly lacks it. The BIC commit object contains only Julian Lam's human author/committer identity and no AI marker. Under the BIC-only rule, later changes and the fix cannot supply AI attribution, so the result is NOT_AI. The advisory's direct fix and release boundary are c0d94a217edcafcdb9b3920a6e80935194bcb19e/v4.15.0; the source diff also reveals that this patch closes the malicious icon.url attribute-breakout route by URI validation but leaves the separately described unescaped tag.name title interpolation unchanged.
